properties.answer: Anthony, 2026-07-27: "go with your recommendation: the interface." Recorded as `dec:pairing-role-placement` (accepted) and `req:complementary-pairing` moved to accepted. The role extends `Interface.designation` rather than becoming a per-node attribute — a Component both publishes and subscribes, so a per-node role collapses to `both` and pairs with everything. AMENDED 2026-07-28 after the dynograph-foundation trial refuted the first draft of the matching key: base-compatibility is `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`, because role-plus-medium alone would pair a consumer requiring REST against a public unauthenticated liveness probe. The gap stays open because the requirement is accepted but NOT YET BUILT — that is the honest state, not an unanswered question.

properties.question: Does the publish/subscribe role belong on the interface itself — extending the `published` flag with a third value meaning "I need one of these from outside" — or on every node, as you described it? Recommendation: the interface. A component both publishes and subscribes, so a single role on a component collapses to `both` and pairs with everything, which is the only reason `both` is needed at all. On an interface, `both` stays rare and means something real.
